stories.t: Crew-12 undocks from the space station for Thursday’s splashdown off California
stories.s: Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway, Sophie Adenot and Andrey Fedyaev pulled away from the station in their SpaceX Dragon at 8:05 a.m. EDT (5:05 a.m. Pacific) this morning after closing the hatch two hours earlier. Splashdown in the Pacific off California is planned for about 8:34 a.m. Pacific Thursday. Five other spacecraft remain docked, including the Crew-13 Dragon.

stories.t: How to use AI visual search on your iPhone, Galaxy or Pixel
stories.s: Apple’s Visual Intelligence in iOS 27 can now search what’s on your screen: take a screenshot with the side and volume-up buttons, then pick Search or Ask (iPhone 15 Pro or newer). On Galaxy phones, turn on Circle to Search under display settings and long-press the home button or bar; Pixel 6 and newer work the same way. Some apps block the feature, and AI answers are worth double-checking.

stories.t: Trump says Iran could ‘take out’ Los Angeles and San Diego; state leaders push back
stories.s: At a campaign stop in Grand Island, Nebraska, on Monday, President Trump told the crowd that Iran “can take out a city” and said to let it hit Los Angeles and San Diego, calling the war’s costs a small price to pay. Gov. Gavin Newsom said the president was advocating an attack on more than 10 million Californians, and the mayors of both cities called the remarks dangerous. At the same event Trump signed an order allowing tax-free purchases of dyed diesel as war-driven fuel prices climb.
stories.w: The Iran war is already driving up gas and diesel prices for Bay Area drivers, and the remarks raise new questions about how Washington views California’s safety.

stories.t: Caltrain weekend ridership runs 50% above pre-pandemic levels
stories.s: Weekend ridership averaged 21,210 in the 2026 fiscal year, up 40.6% from the year before and about 50% above 2019, after weekend service more than doubled to 66 trains a day with the switch to electric trains. Weekday ridership averaged 40,800, up 37.5%, and South San Francisco and Hayward Park are among the stations now above 2019 weekday levels. Caltrain still warns that without new funding it could close more than a third of its stations and drop weekend service.
stories.w: Millbrae’s Caltrain and BART station depends on the weekend and frequent service that the agency says is at risk without new funding.
stories.src: Mountain View Voice (Bay City News), Oct 5, 2026

stories.t: Tech companies fill empty downtown San Francisco storefronts with branded cafes
stories.s: Companies like Zoox, which opened a robotaxi rider lounge near Union Square, an AI insurance startup with its own coffee shop, and Capital One are moving into vacant downtown storefronts. Supporters say the spaces bring foot traffic back to empty blocks, while critics say they cater to tech workers more than to everyone else. At least one of the startup cafes has already stalled, with a Dogpatch location closed shortly after opening.
stories.w: Peninsula commuters heading into the city will see more of these branded spaces as downtown tries to recover its street life.

stories.t: Today in sports: Warriors host the Lakers tonight as 4–0 49ers open as underdogs at Seattle
stories.s: The Warriors, who lost 104–101 to the Clippers in Honolulu on Sunday, host the Lakers in a preseason game tonight at Chase Center, then visit Portland on Wednesday. The unbeaten 49ers open as about three-point underdogs for Sunday’s game at Seattle, only the second time this season they haven’t been favored. The Earthquakes return Sunday at Colorado.

stories.t: 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk expected to miss a few weeks with a knee injury
stories.s: Juszczyk, a 10-time Pro Bowler, hurt his knee in Sunday’s win over Denver, and ESPN reported he could miss a couple of weeks while the team awaited MRI results. Early indications are that he avoided a long-term injury. Reports point to tight end Brayden Willis as a possible fill-in at fullback for the trip to Seattle.

stories.t: Thunder’s Jalen Williams breaks his leg as NBA preseason injuries pile up
stories.s: Oklahoma City forward Jalen Williams fractured his leg and dislocated his ankle and needs surgery, and teammate Cason Wallace has a torn labrum. Orlando’s Jalen Suggs is out about two weeks with a knee bone bruise. Opening weekend also saw Giannis Antetokounmpo debut for Miami, one of several stars, including LeBron James in Philadelphia, playing for new teams this season.

stories.t: Apple TV renews ‘Imperfect Women’ for a second season set on Martha’s Vineyard
stories.s: The thriller, first billed as a limited series, is coming back with an original story rather than another book adaptation. Kerry Washington returns as Eleanor, who goes back to her hometown in Martha’s Vineyard and uncovers secrets about her past. Apple hasn’t set a premiere date or confirmed whether co-stars Elisabeth Moss and Kate Mara will return.

stories.t: Tyler Perry’s ‘Doing Life’ is now streaming on Netflix
stories.s: The drama, which arrived on Netflix Oct. 2, follows a single mother and former prison officer and the ex-convict who once protected her during a riot as they try to rebuild their lives. Naomi Baker and Jay Reeves star. Perry says he drew on real people he has met who kept going through hard circumstances.

stories.t: NASA sets Crew-12’s return: undocking Wednesday, splashdown off California Thursday
stories.s: Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway, ESA’s Sophie Adenot and Roscosmos’ Andrey Fedyaev are scheduled to leave the space station aboard their Dragon at 8:05 a.m. EDT Wednesday, weather permitting. Splashdown is targeted for about 11:34 a.m. EDT Thursday in the Pacific off California, and NASA will stream both. Mission managers are watching weather and recovery-team readiness, so times could shift.

stories.t: New Windows malware uses xAI’s Grok to help it hide on infected PCs
stories.s: Researchers at Qrator found a malware kit called x47.c that steals passwords, browser cookies and AI account keys, and asks Grok to choose how to stay hidden on each computer. It can also drain prepaid AI credits if it finds an API key. Keep Windows updated, never paste commands a website tells you to run, use unique passwords with two-factor sign-in, and set spending limits on any AI accounts.

stories.t: San Mateo County opens three vote centers as Nov. 3 ballots reach mailboxes
stories.s: Ballots for the county’s more than 447,000 registered voters start arriving this week, and three vote centers open today in San Mateo, Redwood City and the South San Francisco Public Library, weekdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. through Nov. 2. The county also has 57 official drop boxes, and more vote centers open with weekend hours on Oct. 24. Mailed ballots must be postmarked by Nov. 3 and arrive by Nov. 10.
stories.w: Millbrae voters can return ballots at any county drop box or vote early at the nearby South San Francisco library starting today.
stories.src: San Mateo County Registration & Elections, Oct 5, 2026

stories.t: Supreme Court opens its new term today with a major climate liability case
stories.s: The justices first hear Suncor and ExxonMobil’s bid to end Boulder, Colorado’s lawsuit seeking damages for local climate costs; the companies argue climate change is a federal matter that states and cities can’t litigate. The term also includes challenges to AR-15-style rifle bans in December, a Colorado Catholic preschool case, and disputes over the administration’s deportation policies. Because many similar suits are pending nationwide, the Boulder ruling could reach well beyond Colorado.
stories.w: Local governments in California, including San Mateo County, have filed similar climate suits against oil companies, so this ruling could decide whether those cases move forward.

stories.t: Bernie Sanders rallies in San Francisco for Prop. 40’s one-time billionaire tax
stories.s: Sen. Bernie Sanders, Rep. Ro Khanna and former Supervisor Jane Kim spoke to hundreds at the Curran Theatre on Saturday night in support of Prop. 40, a one-time 5% tax on California billionaires that would largely fund health care. Gov. Gavin Newsom and Mayor Daniel Lurie oppose it, and opponents have spent more than $80 million, over twice what supporters have raised. Two competing measures, Props. 41 and 42, would cancel it if they pass.
stories.w: Prop. 40 and two rival measures that would cancel it are on the November ballot now arriving in San Mateo County mailboxes.

stories.t: Weekend recap: 49ers move to 4–0 as Warriors open preseason in Honolulu
stories.s: Sunday: 49ers 24, Broncos 14 at Levi’s Stadium, after a 3–3 halftime tie. Also Sunday: Clippers 104, Warriors 101 in the preseason opener in Honolulu. The Earthquakes were idle, and the Giants are not in the postseason. This week: the Warriors host the Lakers on Tuesday at Chase Center and visit Portland on Wednesday; on Sunday (Oct. 11) the 49ers play at Seattle and the Quakes visit Colorado.

stories.t: Kittle’s 56-yard catch-and-run seals the 49ers’ fourth straight win
stories.s: Brock Purdy went 19 of 30 for 218 yards and two touchdowns, and George Kittle’s 56-yard score with about two minutes left put Denver away. Christian McCaffrey ran for 52 yards and a touchdown as the 49ers piled up 140 rushing yards, while Dre Greenlaw had 12 tackles. Mike Evans played through fractured ribs, according to Kittle, as San Francisco heads to Seattle for its first road game since Melbourne.

stories.t: Brewers walk off Padres closer Mason Miller to take a 2–0 NLDS lead
stories.s: With two outs and the bases loaded in the ninth, Jackson Chourio lined a two-run single off Miller, who had walked three batters, to give Milwaukee a 4–3 win in Game 2. The Brewers lead the division series 2–0. Game 3 is Tuesday night at Petco Park in San Diego.

stories.t: ‘Lanterns’ wraps its first season on HBO with Aaron Pierre in the spotlight
stories.s: HBO’s Green Lantern series, co-created by Damon Lindelof, aired its first-season finale, built around Aaron Pierre’s John Stewart, a young recruit. Kyle Chandler co-stars as veteran Hal Jordan, whose death drives much of the season. The finale is streaming on HBO Max for anyone catching up.

stories.t: HARDY’s new single ‘Man in the Box’ swerves from country into rock
stories.s: Country star HARDY released “Man in the Box” late last week, a song that opens as a country track and turns into hard rock in its second half.

stories.t: Space station changes command as Crew-13 settles in and Crew-12 packs for home
stories.s: NASA astronaut Jessica Meir handed command of the International Space Station to Roscosmos cosmonaut Pyotr Dubrov in a ceremony on Sunday. Eleven people are aboard after Crew-13 arrived Oct. 1, with two SpaceX Dragon capsules docked as one crew unpacks and the other prepares to leave. Crew-12’s return to Earth is expected in the coming days.

stories.t: Trump creates a ‘Super Intelligence Force’ to coordinate federal AI policy
stories.s: President Trump announced a new team of senior officials, reporting to him and chief of staff Susie Wiles, to keep the U.S. ahead in what the administration now calls “Super Intelligence.” It will coordinate outreach to tech companies, infrastructure providers and community and religious groups. It follows a Sept. 29 White House summit where AI company leaders signed a voluntary accord; the administration has opposed formal guardrails on the technology.

stories.t: SFO shifts departures back to its north-facing runways
stories.s: With six months of work on Runway 1R finished, SFO planned to move most departures back to Runways 1L and 1R starting Saturday, though weather and high winds can still push them onto the west-facing 28 runways. The airport expects about 45 to 48 arrivals an hour in good conditions, up from a low of 36, while low-visibility capacity stays near 36; the roughly $215 million project included $92.1 million in federal money.
stories.w: Millbrae and San Bruno neighbors should see departure patterns return to normal, and travelers should expect Fleet Week to affect SFO traffic on the afternoons of Oct. 8–12.

stories.t: Fleet Week opens; BART adds longer trains for next weekend’s air shows
stories.s: San Francisco Fleet Week runs today through Oct. 12, with air shows from noon to 4 p.m. next Saturday and Sunday, Oct. 10 and 11. BART will run longer trains on both air show days and Muni is adding service, with Embarcadero and Montgomery St. stations connecting to buses and streetcars bound for Pier 39, Fort Mason, Marina Green and Crissy Field.
stories.w: Peninsula residents can ride BART from Millbrae or other stations, where weekend parking is free, instead of hunting for parking near the crowded waterfront.

stories.t: Today in sports: 49ers host Broncos, Warriors open preseason in Honolulu
stories.s: The 3-0 49ers host the Denver Broncos at 1:25 p.m. at Levi’s Stadium on CBS. The Warriors open a six-game preseason against the Clippers at 4 p.m. Pacific at the Stan Sheriff Center in Honolulu, streaming on the Golden State app and NBA League Pass, with a projected lineup of Steph Curry, Brandin Podziemski, Yaxel Lendeborg, Draymond Green and Al Horford. The Earthquakes are next in action Oct. 10.

stories.t: 49ers rule out Bosa and Mykel Williams; Evans questionable vs. Denver
stories.s: The 49ers ruled out defensive ends Nick Bosa (knee, calf) and Mykel Williams (knee) and defensive tackle James Thompson (ankle) for today’s game against Denver. Receiver Mike Evans (ribs), linebackers Dre Greenlaw and Jaden Dugger, and edge rusher Keion White are questionable, while Christian McCaffrey and Trent Williams practiced fully; Denver ruled out linebacker Dondrea Tillman (hamstring).

stories.t: Kerr limits Curry, Green and Horford to the first half of the preseason opener
stories.s: Steve Kerr said Curry, Green and Horford will play only the first half, about 12 to 16 minutes, and every player, including the three two-way players, will get minutes against the Clippers. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are still rehabbing and Kristaps Porziņģis stayed home with a health issue; the Warriors host the Lakers at Chase Center on Tuesday at 7 p.m., then play at Portland on Wednesday.

stories.t: Verity rules the Friday box office
stories.s: The Colleen Hoover adaptation Verity, with Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson, took in about $15 million on its opening Friday from 3,510 theaters. That was roughly four times the next film, the holdover Resident Evil at about $3.6 million, putting Verity on pace to top the weekend; full weekend numbers arrive Sunday and Monday.

stories.t: Digger stumbles with a third-place Friday
stories.s: Tom Cruise’s Digger earned about $3.5 million on its first Friday from 3,321 theaters, finishing third behind Verity and Resident Evil and just ahead of Heart of the Beast. That start puts the costly Iñárritu satire at risk of falling short of the $12 million to $15 million weekend Warner Bros. had projected.

stories.t: Crew-12 heads home no earlier than Wednesday, with splashdown off California
stories.s: NASA and SpaceX are targeting undocking of Crew-12 (NASA’s Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA’s Sophie Adenot and Roscosmos’ Andrey Fedyaev) no earlier than 1:05 a.m. EDT Wednesday, Oct. 7, after reviewing weather and splashdown conditions off the California coast. That’s later than the Monday date mentioned earlier; before leaving, the crew hands its duties to the newly arrived Crew-13, and Meir is scheduled to pass station command to cosmonaut Pyotr Dubrov today.

stories.t: Pentagon sends a third carrier group to the Middle East
stories.s: The Pentagon is deploying a third carrier strike group and up to 10,000 sailors and Marines to the Middle East. President Trump said renewed strikes on Iran are possible after the midterm elections.
stories.w: Wider conflict with Iran could push up oil prices that flow through to Peninsula gas pumps, and Bay Area military families may see loved ones deployed.

stories.t: Brazil votes Sunday in Lula vs. Flávio Bolsonaro race
stories.s: Brazilians vote Sunday in a presidential race between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the former president. If no one wins a majority, the top two will meet in a runoff on Oct. 25.
stories.w: The result will shape U.S. ties with one of the hemisphere’s largest economies and matters to Bay Area residents with family in Brazil.

stories.t: Trump opens a red-state campaign swing ahead of the midterms
stories.s: Trump started a campaign tour through Texas and Oklahoma, backing Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton, who is reportedly trailing Democrat James Talarico. Outside groups have poured heavy spending into Paxton’s campaign.
stories.w: Control of the U.S. Senate, decided Nov. 3 alongside California’s own races, will shape federal decisions on immigration, disaster aid and transit money that reach San Mateo County.

stories.t: Today in sports: Warriors wrap Hawaii camp before Sunday’s opener
stories.s: The Warriors close their training camp at BYU–Hawaii today, with newcomers such as Yaxel Lendeborg getting their first looks, before facing the Clippers on Sunday in Honolulu. The 3-0 49ers host the Broncos on Sunday at 1:25 p.m. on CBS. The Earthquakes are next in action Oct. 10, and the Giants are in their offseason.

stories.t: Mike Evans and Nick Bosa sit out 49ers practice before Denver game
stories.s: Receiver Mike Evans (ribs) and defensive end Nick Bosa (knee, calf) didn’t practice Thursday, along with Dre Greenlaw, KhaDarel Hodge, James Thompson and Keion White, as the 49ers prepared for Denver. Left tackle Trent Williams returned on a limited basis after a neck stinger in Week 3, and Evans was seen working on the side; Friday’s report sets game statuses for Sunday.

stories.t: Victoria Monét’s Frequency of Love arrives, with her tour ending in San Francisco
stories.s: Monét’s second studio album, a 22-track set on Lovett Music/RCA, features Bruno Mars, SZA, Bryson Tiller, Leon Thomas, Lucky Daye, Chlöe and her daughter Hazel, and borrows from R&B classics by Marvin Gaye and Tammi Terrell, the Isley Brothers and Brandy. Her Frequency of Love Tour opens Oct. 27 in Raleigh and wraps Dec. 17 in San Francisco.

stories.t: Warner Bros. answers Digger critics with a ‘decide for yourself’ ad
stories.s: New since Friday’s release: Warner Bros. posted a 27-second spot pairing raves and pans and telling moviegoers to make up their own minds, with Digger hovering around 52% on Rotten Tomatoes. Some trackers projected an opening as low as $7.5 million from about 3,500 theaters, below the studio’s own $12 million to $15 million estimate, and Variety reported the budget grew to $160 million to $180 million.

stories.t: Webb finds clues to the planet-smashing collisions that build worlds like ours
stories.s: A team led by Kate Su of the Space Science Institute used Webb and archived Spitzer data to study 21 rare young star systems with unusually warm, dusty disks left by giant collisions. About a third are silica-rich, likely from violent impacts between Mars-sized bodies around stars younger than 300 million years, roughly when Earth and the Moon formed; the rest point to gentler grazing collisions. The study appeared Thursday in The Astrophysical Journal.

stories.t: Anthropic commits $100 million to train 10,000 AI engineers
stories.s: Anthropic launched Claude Frontier Academy, pledging $100 million to train 10,000 engineers by the end of 2027 to put its Claude AI to work inside their organizations. The first program pairs an in-person course with a 12-week residency on a real project, with cohorts in San Francisco, New York and London and early participants including Accenture, Deloitte and Morgan Stanley.

stories.t: Saturn reaches opposition Sunday, visible all night
stories.s: Saturn reaches opposition on Sunday, rising around sunset and staying up most of the night, which makes it an easy target this weekend. Later this month, a thin crescent Moon sits near Jupiter before dawn on Oct. 6, and the Orionid meteor shower peaks Oct. 21–22, best seen before dawn after moonset.

stories.t: Voters will decide a $7.5 billion science research bond in 2028
stories.s: New since Thursday’s wrap-up: Newsom’s last signature of the session, made atop the Golden Gate Bridge, went on SB 895, which asks voters in March 2028 to approve a $7.5 billion bond for a state foundation funding peer-reviewed scientific and health research. In his final session he signed more than 1,000 bills and vetoed 120, for about 8,000 signed over eight years; he leaves office in January and says he may still call special sessions.
stories.w: Bay Area universities, hospitals and the South San Francisco biotech cluster would be among the biggest competitors for the research money if voters approve it.

stories.t: Pentagon creates a new command for autonomous drones and robots
stories.s: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth announced a new four-star command, called AutoWarCom, to rapidly expand the military’s use of autonomous drones and robots. He also said the Pentagon will cut 20% of its generals and admirals.
stories.w: Bay Area tech and robotics companies could see new defense work from the push, along with renewed debate over military uses of AI built in Silicon Valley.

stories.t: Judge to review the secret legal basis for military boat strikes
stories.s: A federal judge will examine the Pentagon’s secret legal justification for its lethal strikes on boats, which have killed more than 200 people. After reviewing it, the judge will decide whether the reasoning should be made public.
stories.w: Californians following the military’s expanding use of force could learn how the government justifies the strikes, a question that may shape oversight debates in Congress.

stories.t: Today in sports: 49ers lead the NFC West as Warriors train in Hawaii
stories.s: The 49ers sit alone atop the NFC West at 3-0 after last Sunday’s 36-30 win over Arizona and host the Broncos this Sunday at 1:25 p.m. at Levi’s Stadium. The Warriors are midway through training camp at BYU–Hawaii, which runs through Saturday, ahead of Sunday’s preseason opener against the Clippers in Honolulu. The Earthquakes are idle until Oct. 10, and the Giants are in their offseason.

stories.t: Kerr installs a five-out offense at Warriors camp
stories.s: Steve Kerr used the first practice in Laie to install a five-out offense, saying the Warriors must keep up with how the league has changed after years of playing two big men. He plans to keep Steph Curry and Draymond Green together in the starting lineup and would like Al Horford off the bench for 18 to 20 minutes, but Kristaps Porziņģis didn’t travel to Hawaii and is out indefinitely with a health issue.

stories.t: New this weekend: Verity and Digger hit theaters, plus Miranda Lambert’s disco turn
stories.s: In theaters, Amazon MGM’s Verity with Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson is tracking for $35 million or more and the No. 1 spot, while Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s Digger, starring Tom Cruise, is projected at $12 million to $15 million against a $125 million budget. On streaming, Netflix’s seven-part East of Eden with Florence Pugh and HBO’s legal drama War with Dominic West and Sienna Miller premiered Thursday. New albums out today include Miranda Lambert’s Crisco, Victoria Monét’s Frequency of Love and Johnny Marr’s The Age of Everything, and the Hardly Strictly Bluegrass festival plays Golden Gate Park this weekend.

stories.t: Miranda Lambert goes country-disco on new album Crisco
stories.s: Lambert’s 11th album, out today on MCA Nashville, blends country with late-’70s and early-’80s disco strings across 12 tracks. It features Ella Langley on opener “Snakeskin Boots,” Chris Stapleton on “A Song to Sing” and a cover of Jim Croce’s “I’ll Have to Say I Love You in a Song”; RIFF gave it 8 out of 10, calling it a fun showcase of a veteran at ease.

stories.t: Crew-13 docks at the space station
stories.s: A Falcon 9 lifted off from Cape Canaveral at 11:10 a.m. EDT Thursday, its first stage landed back at the Cape, and the Dragon docked to the station’s Harmony module at 7 p.m. EDT. NASA’s Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, Canada’s Joshua Kutryk and Russia’s Sergey Teteryatnikov floated aboard after the hatch opened at 9:19 p.m., joining the seven-member Expedition 75 crew.

stories.t: Microsoft-linked data center ran gas generators without permits, report finds
stories.s: An investigation found that a Microsoft-linked data center in Vineland, New Jersey, ran dozens of gas-fired generators without permits for nearly a year, releasing large amounts of smog-forming pollution. The finding adds to questions about how the rush to build computing capacity for AI and cloud services is being powered.

stories.t: Newsom wraps up his last bill-signing season as governor
stories.s: Gov. Gavin Newsom signed and vetoed his last bills as governor by Wednesday’s deadline, working through a final batch of 1,160 measures and nearly 8,000 over his time in office. New laws include a 13-bill youth online safety package that bars social media companies from offering addictive features such as infinite scroll to users under 16, a ban on child marriage, stronger state antitrust powers, tax credits for local news outlets and a ban on public officials issuing crypto meme coins.
stories.w: Peninsula families with teens will see new limits on how social apps can hook kids, and struggling local newsrooms that cover San Mateo County could tap the new tax credits.

stories.t: Bay Area warm spell could last into mid-October
stories.s: Above-normal temperatures that arrived Tuesday are expected to hang on, with the 70s in San Francisco and the mid-80s to 90s inland, and a National Weather Service forecaster said the warmth could run into the middle of October. The coast should stay in the 60s and low 70s, and fire danger will be elevated, though strong winds aren’t in the forecast. San Francisco could see its first October streak of 10 straight 70-degree days since 2015.
stories.w: Bayside and inland Peninsula neighborhoods should expect warm afternoons for days: drink water, check on heat-sensitive neighbors and avoid anything that could spark a fire.

stories.t: Supreme Court lets third-country deportations resume for now
stories.s: On Tuesday the Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to keep deporting people to countries other than their own while the justices decide whether migrants must first get a meaningful chance to object. The order pauses an appeals court ruling that federal attorneys said had forced the cancellation of a flight carrying about 70 people. The administration has sent about 25,000 people to more than two dozen countries, most of them to Mexico.
stories.w: San Mateo County is home to many immigrant families, and relatives facing removal could be sent to countries where they have no ties while the case plays out.

stories.t: Last U.S. troops leave Iraq, ending the anti-ISIS mission there
stories.s: The Pentagon said the last U.S. troops deployed for the fight against ISIS have left Iraq, departing Erbil Air Base in the Kurdistan region with their equipment. The task force has moved to Jordan, hundreds of U.S. troops remain in Syria, and the U.S. will keep offering training and intelligence support. Kurdish officials warned the pullout leaves their region exposed to Iranian strikes and a possible ISIS comeback.
stories.w: It closes a chapter that began in 2003 and touched many California military families, while U.S. forces in Jordan and Syria stay close to tensions with Iran.

stories.t: Today in sports: unbeaten 49ers turn to Denver
stories.s: The 49ers are 3-0 and alone atop the NFC West after Sunday’s 36-30 win over Arizona, when Brock Purdy threw for 297 yards and four touchdowns; Denver visits Levi’s Stadium this Sunday at 1:25 p.m. on CBS. The Warriors opened training camp at BYU–Hawaii in Laie this week ahead of their preseason opener against the Clippers on Sunday in Honolulu. The Earthquakes beat Portland 3-1 on Saturday and next play Oct. 10, while the Giants’ season is over.

stories.t: Giants stand by Vitello after a 97-loss season
stories.s: Buster Posey gave manager Tony Vitello a vote of confidence after a first season that ended with 97 losses and the Giants missing the playoffs for the ninth time in 10 years. Posey took the blame for a bullpen that blew 27 saves and said adding dependable relievers is the top offseason priority; the team also expects Randy Rodríguez back from Tommy John surgery next season.

stories.t: Tom Cruise’s Digger splits critics ahead of Friday’s opening
stories.s: Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s oil-industry satire, starring Tom Cruise as tycoon Digger Rockwell alongside John Goodman and Riz Ahmed, sat at 53% on Rotten Tomatoes as reviews rolled in. BBC Culture praised it as an art-house spectacle, while IndieWire likened it to a big-budget Dr. Strangelove riff that feels cut off from real human truth. It opens in theaters Friday.

stories.t: Early Verity review calls the Colleen Hoover thriller a twisty, fun ride
stories.s: Michael Showalter’s adaptation of Colleen Hoover’s best-seller stars Dakota Johnson as a broke writer hired to ghostwrite a famous author’s series, and Anne Hathaway as the injured novelist whose remote Vermont home hides a disturbing confession. Time Out gave it three of five stars, calling it a mostly fun ride that still piles on one twist too many. It opens in theaters Friday.

stories.t: SpaceX Crew-13 set to launch to the space station this morning
stories.s: NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins (commander) and Luke Delaney (pilot), Canada’s Joshua Kutryk and Russia’s Sergey Teteryatnikov are scheduled to lift off at 11:10 a.m. EDT (8:10 a.m. Pacific) on a Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral. Forecasters gave a 55% chance of acceptable weather, with scattered showers possible, and NASA will stream the launch and docking.

stories.t: California adds new AI rules for workplaces, health care and deepfakes
stories.s: Newsom signed 13 AI bills on Wednesday: employers can’t rely only on AI to discipline or fire workers, must disclose when AI drives a mass layoff, and can’t put surveillance tools in workplace bathrooms. Other laws protect doctors’ judgment when AI tools are used in care, bar stripping digital watermarks from AI content, and require gene synthesis companies to screen orders, including Peninsula legislators’ bills SB 1000 (Sen. Josh Becker) and AB 1864 (Asm. Marc Berman).
